title: Buying a House in the Wichita Area | Alexander Colón
description: What buying a house around Wichita actually costs and what order it happens in. Read it first, ask Alex second, decide when you are ready.
h1: Buying a house here, explained before you are asked to decide anything
job: Give a first time buyer enough of the process for free that asking Alex a question feels like the small next step it is.
primaryPrinciple: Commitment ladder. A low friction micro conversion first, never the big ask cold.

bands.headline: Buying a house here, explained before you are asked to decide anything
bands.support: Most of the stress in a first purchase comes from finding out what something costs on the day it is due. This page is the part that usually gets skipped.

bands.eyebrow: Before you talk to a lender
bands.heading: Ask Wick a question first
bands.intro: Wick knows the buying process on this page cold: pre approval, what money moves when, what happens at inspection. Ask before you call a lender or Alex, and it will say so the moment it does not know something.

bands.heading: The order things actually happen in
bands.intro: Six stages, and the money leaves your account at three of them. Knowing which three is most of what makes this manageable.

steps.title: Get pre approved
steps.detail: A lender looks at your income, your debts, and your credit, and tells you what you can borrow. It costs nothing and it is the step that turns a price range from a guess into a number. Alex can point you at lenders who work this market, and you are free to use your own.

steps.title: Work out what you actually want
steps.detail: Not a wish list. The two or three things that would make you regret the purchase if they were missing, separated from the things you would like. This conversation saves more time than any search filter.

steps.title: See houses
steps.detail: Alex walks them with you and points out what a house is telling you about itself. The point of this stage is to get you calibrated, so by the fifth house you can read one yourself.

steps.title: Make an offer
steps.detail: Price is one term of several. The closing date, the possession date, what stays with the house, and how the inspection is handled all move, and some of them matter more than the number does. This is where earnest money leaves your account.

steps.title: Inspection and appraisal
steps.detail: You pay for the inspection. The lender orders the appraisal and you pay for that too. Between them they are the two places a deal most often gets renegotiated, and Alex will tell you which findings are worth reopening and which are just the age of the house.

steps.title: Close
steps.detail: You sign, the remaining funds move, and you get keys. The closing figure is known days ahead, so nothing about the last step should be a surprise by the time you get there.

bands.heading: The money, in the order it leaves your account
body: Earnest money goes first, at the offer, and it is credited back to you at closing rather than spent. The inspection is paid at the time of the inspection. Closing costs come last and they are the largest of the three, and your lender is required to put them in writing before you get there.

The exact figures depend on the price of the house and the loan you use, which is why nobody honest will quote them to you off a web page. What you can do right now is ask a lender for the numbers on a specific price, and ask Alex to sanity check what comes back.

bands.line: Already talked to a lender and just have a question for Alex?

bands.heading: Work backward from the payment, not the price
body: Most people start with a price and hope the payment works out. It is easier the other way around: decide what you are comfortable paying every month, then see what price that supports.
The rate field is blank because this page will not quote you one. Use the rate a lender actually gave you and the answer means something.

items.q: How much do I need saved before I start?
items.a: It depends on the loan. Some loan types are built around a small down payment and some are not, and the down payment is only one of three places money leaves your account. Ask a lender to run it on a specific price, then ask Alex whether the answer looks right for this market.
Agent compensation comes out of the transaction and it is put in writing before you sign anything. You will see the number and agree to it in advance, and nothing about it is a surprise at closing.

items.q: How long does the whole thing take?
items.a: The part you control is how long you look, which varies enormously. The part after an accepted offer is driven by the lender and the title work. Alex will give you the current realistic window when you ask, rather than a number from a template.

items.q: What if my credit is not great?
items.a: Talk to a lender before you assume anything. People rule themselves out on this more often than lenders do, and the fix is sometimes a few months of specific, boring steps rather than years.

bands.heading: What buyers say about working with Alex
Ask the question you have been sitting on
bands.body: You do not need to be ready to buy to ask something. Most of the useful conversations Alex has are with people who are months out.
